items.title: Domination of a map is equivalent to universal injectivity of the pushout
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for maps f and g out of a common module M, the map g dominates f exactly when the pushout map f' is universally injective (statement lines 21152-21163, with the pushout square drawn in the statement). The proof does not construct the dominating factorisation: it recalls that the pushout is a quotient of a direct sum, writes down the resulting short exact sequence of kernels of f, g and f', transports it along tensoring with an arbitrary module using that tensoring commutes with pushouts, and then reads the two conditions off the same sequence (proof lines 21165-21183). Getting both sides into one kernel sequence is the content of the argument. H2.
